layerCompletionEvidence.conclusion: objective progress is per layer with a compile-time layer key; there is no dynamic layer list

layerCompletionEvidence.evidence: WardenObjectiveManager.OnStateChange -> OnObjectiveChainUpdated(layer, chainIndex) (verified edge, three call sites) and -> UpdateEventStep(layer, oldState, newState) (verified edge); CheckWardenObjectiveStatus takes old and new chainIndex plus old and new eWardenSubObjectiveStatus.
layerCompletionEvidence.conclusion: the per-layer phase is chainIndex (byte) and the sub-phase is eWardenSubObjectiveStatus; both advance inside the status machine, not through a separate API

layerCompletionEvidence.evidence: eWardenObjectiveStatus (dump line 589295) NotDiscovered 0 / Discovered 10 / Started 20 / WardenObjectivePartiallySolved 30 / WardenObjectiveItemSolved 40; WardenObjectiveManager.ForceCompleteObjective(LG_LayerType) 0x1515380 and ForceCompleteObjectiveAll(LG_LayerType) 0x1515270; OnWinConditionSolved(LG_LayerType, bool) 0x151C330; ActivateWinCondition() 0x150F710 called by CheckWardenObjectiveStatus (verified edge).
layerCompletionEvidence.conclusion: per-layer completion is the status transition to WardenObjectiveItemSolved for that layer, forced through AttemptInteract/ForceCompleteObjective; the layer key tells main from secondary from third

layerCompletionEvidence.evidence: the string Overload only occurs in the .NET reflection/command tables of the dump; the objective layer model, the state struct and LG_LayerType never use it.
layerCompletionEvidence.conclusion: the catalog word overload has no native identifier; it can only be mapped onto third_* / LG_LayerType.ThirdLayer by convention, which is an assumption and not evidence

layerCompletionEvidence.evidence: WardenObjectiveManager.CheckExpeditionSuccess() 0x15124F0 / CheckExpeditionFailed() 0x15123B0 (no direct caller decoded), ElevatorShaftLanding win-condition callbacks, ElevatorRide.StartElevatorRide 0x1678BB0, ExpeditionEndState enum, GS_ExpeditionSuccess/Fail/Abort state classes whose methods are shared stubs.

catalogMismatches: the objective triggers have no resource output port, but the current catalog still declares resource outputs (objective/alarm/scan) on every objective trigger row; the rows also declare no handle output yet.
forge.trigger.objective.scan_paused and forge.action.map.scan_pause have no native counterpart: eBioscanStatus has no paused value and pBioscanState has no pause flag.
forge.trigger.objective.scan_failed maps only onto eBioscanStatus.TimedOut, which is a timeout, not a documented failure; failure semantics must be defined by Forge.
forge.action.map.scan_progress has no native setter; the catalog row implies an amount/rate write that the game does not expose.
forge.action.map.scan_path has no native entry at all.

forge.trigger.objective.alarm_started/stopped and scan_started are the same native instance kind (ChainedPuzzleInstance); the catalog splits them into two resources, while the game distinguishes them by ChainedPuzzleDataBlock.TriggerAlarmOnActivate and ChainedPuzzleComponent.PuzzleType.
unproven: Every host/client claim: no body was executed and no runtime log was captured. The side values rest on state-replicator interfaces and Master_/Sync naming only.
Call frequency of UpdateFromInLevel, Mastermind.UpdateEvents and CP_Bioscan_Core.Update: no direct caller exists in the image, so the poll rate is unknown.
Whether OnStateChange runs before or after the native state is applied on a client, and whether it is invoked on the host for locally produced changes.
Exact meaning of CP_Bioscan_Core.SetTimeOut/SetTimeIn and of eBioscanStatus.Waiting versus TimedOut.
Whether ChainedPuzzleInstance.OnStateChange fires for a solved alarm before or after the wave stop it performs through Mastermind.TryGetEvent.
